fields.statement: Verified at 2d58ab91 by reading the diff and running scoped tests. go test -trimpath ./internal/usage/... passes: TestLiveLimit (49% of 4900 tokens gives 10000, i.e. tokens/0.49; none under 1%, with 0 or negative tokens), TestLiveWindowAndLiveness (Start = resets_at minus kind length; not live at or after resets_at). From a checkout outside ~/code, go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestUsageWindowsHitKinds|TestUsageLiveLimit|TestHealthUsage|TestUsageHold' passes. TestUsageLiveLimit uses a fake clock and fake adapter: the live 2000 beats setting 1000 and learned 900 (no hold at 1100 used); the window comes from the snapshot, with used counted to now; a lower live 1111 holds and a raised one lifts it; an expired snapshot falls back to setting 1000, then learned 900; under 1% gives no limit; a recorded limit hit still holds through governorHold. The hold is recomputed each poll (prepare keeps no hold state), so setting 1000 holding without a live limit and not holding with live 2000 shows a raised live limit lifts a hold the setting caused. TestHealthUsageLiveLimit with weekly=777 reports 'weekly 0 of 2000' and never 777. usageLimit is live, then setting, then learned, and both usageHoldOf and healthUsage call it. TestLimitHits/TestLearnedLimit* pass. Note: TestUsageWindowsHitKinds fails when run inside ~/code (the rhiza root redirects limitsDir), but the parent commit fails the same way there, so this commit did not cause it.
